claim: An obstacle pushes a bird away in proportion to how deep inside its radius the bird is, and leaves birds beyond it alone.
derivation: Only the obstacle rule is on (w_o = 3, R_o = 3.4). One obstacle sits at (12, 10).
A (10, 10) moving (1, 0) is 2 from the obstacle: push = 3 · (3.4 − 2) = 4.2 along −δ/|δ| = (−1, 0), so O_A = (−4.2, 0) (E7).
v′_A = (1 − 4.2/60, 0) = (0.93, 0) and x′_A = 10 + 0.93/60 = 10.0155 (E9, E10). Obstacles have no damping term, unlike the steering rules.
B (20, 20) is 12.81 from the obstacle, beyond R_o, so it keeps (0, 1) and moves to (20, 20.016667).
